title: Automated Coral Detection and Instance Segmentation in Underwater Imagery: Evaluating YOLO Model Performance and transferability to Mesophotic Coral Ecosystems
content: Automated coral image analysis remains challenging because methods must resolve individual colonies while preserving taxonomic information. We present a YOLO-based instance-segmentation framework trained on more than 9,500 hand-annotated images of Caribbean scleractinian corals representing 57 species and 22 genera. Four architectures, YOLOv8x, YOLOv9e, YOLOv11x, and YOLOv12x, were evaluated under consistent training conditions at both species and genus levels. On the internal test set, species-level mAP₅₀ reached 0.854 and genus-level mAP₅₀ reached 0.883, with inference times of ap-proximately 4–6 ms per image. YOLOv8x and YOLOv11x provided the strongest overall balance of precision, recall, segmentation accuracy, and speed, while YOLOv12x showed no consistent improvement despite added architectural complexity. Segmentation per-formance varied among taxa and growth forms, with compact or visually distinct colonies generally producing stronger masks than branching, encrusting, low-contrast, or sub-strate-integrated forms. External model transfer was evaluated on independent meso-photic coral ecosystem imagery using published results and expert review. Ex-pert-confirmed precision was higher at genus level than species level and increased with confidence filtering, reaching 82.8% for genus-level and 71.1% for species-level predic-tions at confidence >0.90. These results indicate that YOLO-based instance segmentation can produce rapid, taxonomically resolved coral observations, but external applications require confidence-based filtering and expert review, particularly for species-level in-ference in visually complex reef imagery.
